name: Maple Roasted Carrots
flavorProfile: Sweet and caramelized at the edges, with the maple browning rather than sitting on top.
healthBenefit: Beta-carotene from the carrots, which the body converts to vitamin A, and a roasting method that needs very little added fat to work.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the carrot sticks with the olive oil, maple syrup, salt and pepper until they are evenly coated.
Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet, leaving space between the pieces so they roast instead of steaming.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once halfway through, until the edges are browned and a fork slides in easily.

name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Lemon
flavorProfile: Nutty and crisp on the cut side, sharpened by lemon juice added off the heat.
healthBenefit: A cruciferous vegetable with fiber and vitamin K, roasted rather than boiled so the flavor compounds stay in the pan instead of the water.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the halved sprouts with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Lay them cut side down on a baking sheet, which is what gives you the browned face.
Roast for 20 to 24 minutes, until the cut sides are deep brown and the outer leaves have crisped.
Squeeze the lemon juice over them as soon as they come out of the oven.

name: Cinnamon Roasted Butternut Squash
flavorProfile: Soft and sweet inside, with warm cinnamon and a little salt keeping it from tasting like dessert.
healthBenefit: One of the densest vitamin A sources in the vegetable aisle, with potassium and fiber alongside it.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400F (200C).
Toss the squash cubes with the olive oil, cinnamon, salt and pepper on a baking sheet and spread them out in one layer.
Roast for 15 minutes, turn the cubes, then roast for 15 to 20 minutes more, until they are tender and browned in spots.

name: Roasted Beets with Orange
flavorProfile: Earthy and sweet, cut through by orange juice stirred in at the end.
healthBenefit: Beets carry dietary nitrates and folate, and the vitamin C in the orange helps with the iron the beets bring.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the beet cubes with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Wrap them loosely in foil or cover the baking dish, so they steam as they roast and stay moist.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, until a knife goes through without resistance.
Uncover, pour the orange juice over them, and stir to coat.

name: Roasted Fennel and Red Pepper
flavorProfile: The anise edge of raw fennel turns mild and sweet in the oven, and the pepper adds color and juice.
healthBenefit: Fennel brings fiber and potassium, and red bell pepper is one of the highest vitamin C vegetables by weight.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the sliced fennel and red pepper with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spread them on a baking sheet in one layer.
Roast for 22 to 26 minutes, until the fennel edges have browned and the pepper has softened.

name: Rosemary Roasted Turnips
flavorProfile: Peppery when raw, mellow and faintly sweet once roasted, with rosemary crisping against the cut faces.
healthBenefit: A lower-starch root than potato, with vitamin C and fiber, useful when you want a roasted root without the carbohydrate load.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the turnip cubes with the olive oil, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Spread them on a baking sheet in one layer.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the outsides are browned and the middles are soft.

name: Baked Sweet Potato Wedges
flavorProfile: Crisp along the skin, soft through the middle, salted while still hot.
healthBenefit: Vitamin A and fiber, with the skin left on, which is where a good share of the fiber sits.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Scrub the sweet potato and cut it into wedges, leaving the skin on.
Toss the wedges with the olive oil and pepper.
Lay them skin side down on a baking sheet and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the edges are browned.
Salt them while they are still hot, so it sticks.

name: Garlic Roasted Zucchini
flavorProfile: Browned on the cut faces, garlicky, and light enough to sit beside anything.
healthBenefit: A high-water, low-calorie vegetable that adds volume to a plate, with potassium and a little vitamin C.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the zucchini with the olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper.
Spread the pieces on a baking sheet without overlapping them, or the zucchini will release water and steam.
Roast for 18 to 22 minutes, until the cut faces have browned.

name: Sautéed Kale with Lemon
flavorProfile: Softened but still with some chew, garlicky, finished with lemon juice off the heat.
healthBenefit: Kale carries vitamin K, vitamin C and calcium, and the lemon juice added at the end keeps the vitamin C from cooking away.
instructions: Strip the kale leaves off their stems and tear them into pieces.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the garlic for about 30 seconds, until it smells sweet.
Add the kale, the salt and the pepper, and turn it with tongs for 4 to 6 minutes, until it has wilted and darkened.
Take the pan off the heat and squeeze the lemon juice over the top.

name: Braised Cabbage with Apple
flavorProfile: Sweet and slightly tart, cooked down until the cabbage is silky and the apple has gone soft.
healthBenefit: Cabbage fiber plus apple pectin, a soluble fiber that feeds gut bacteria, in a dish that cooks gently enough to stay easy on digestion.
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a lidded pan over medium heat and cook the shredded cabbage, stirring, until it starts to soften.
Add the diced apple, the salt, the sugar, the water and the cider vinegar.
Cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour, stirring now and then and adding a splash more water if the pan runs dry, until the cabbage is very soft.

name: Garlicky Green Beans
flavorProfile: Still snappy in the middle, tossed warm in a dressing of lemon, garlic, mustard and thyme.
healthBenefit: Fiber, vitamin K and folate, cooked briefly so the beans keep their texture and their vitamin C.
instructions: Trim the stem ends off the beans.
In a bowl, whisk the lemon juice, grated garlic, mustard, salt and pepper, then stir in the thyme leaves.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat, add the beans and the water, cover and cook for about 5 minutes, until tender with a little bite.
Tip the beans into the bowl and toss them with the dressing.

name: Skillet Asparagus with Lemon
flavorProfile: Grassy and bright, cooked just long enough to lose the raw edge.
healthBenefit: Asparagus carries folate and inulin, a prebiotic fiber that gut bacteria ferment, and it cooks in under five minutes.
instructions: Snap or cut the woody ends off the asparagus.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Lay the spears in one layer and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, rolling them once, until they are bright green and lightly browned.
Season with the salt and pepper, take the pan off the heat, and squeeze the lemon juice over them.

name: Sautéed Leeks and Carrots
flavorProfile: Gentle and sweet, the leek going soft and silky while the carrot keeps a little bite.
healthBenefit: Leeks bring prebiotic fructans that feed gut bacteria, and the carrot adds beta-carotene, which absorbs better with the oil present.
instructions: Slice the leek into rings and rinse them well, since grit collects between the layers. Dice the carrot small and slice the onion.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and soften the onion for about 3 minutes.
Add the carrot and cook for about 5 minutes over medium low heat.
Add the leek and the salt, stir, cover and cook gently for about 20 minutes, until everything is tender. Finish with the pepper.

name: Broccoli Sautéed with Garlic and Ginger
flavorProfile: Warm ginger and garlic against bright green broccoli, blanched and sautéed fast so the florets stay firm.
healthBenefit: Broccoli is a source of sulforaphane precursors and vitamin C, and a short cook keeps more of both than boiling does.

ingredients.prepNote: florets, stems peeled and cut into bite-size pieces

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the sea salt.
Add the broccoli and blanch it for 30 seconds.
Drain the broccoli and rinse it under cold water to stop the cooking and keep it green.
Heat the olive oil in a sauté pan over medium heat. Add the ginger and garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Stir in the broccoli and the pinch of salt and sauté for 2 minutes. The broccoli should still be firm. Serve right away.

name: Roasted Turmeric Cauliflower
flavorProfile: Golden all over, earthy from the turmeric, with browned crisp edges on the flat faces.
healthBenefit: A cruciferous vegetable with fiber and vitamin C, roasted with turmeric, whose curcumin absorbs better alongside fat.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400F (200C).
Toss the cauliflower with the olive oil in a bowl until it is well coated, then add the garlic, turmeric, cumin and salt and toss again.
Spread it on a baking sheet in one layer.
Roast for 20 minutes, turn the pieces, then roast for 10 to 20 minutes more, until tender, golden and crisp at the edges.
Scatter the cilantro over the top if you are using it.

name: Lemon Brown Rice with Parsley
flavorProfile: Nutty and chewy, loosened with lemon juice and parsley stirred through at the end.
healthBenefit: Whole-grain rice keeps its bran, which is where the fiber, magnesium and B vitamins are, and the lemon goes in off the heat.

ingredients.prepNote: a sixth of a leaf, cooked with the rice and removed
a pinch for the rice, the rest in the dressing

instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put it in a pot with the water, the bay leaf and a pinch of the salt, and bring it to a boil.
Lower the heat to medium-low, cover, and keep it at a gentle simmer for about 45 minutes, skimming off any foam, until the water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for 15 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and fluff the rice with a fork.
Pulse the parsley, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic and the rest of the salt in a food processor until finely chopped but still textured.
Fold the dressing through the rice, mix in the lemon zest, season with the pepper and serve warm.

name: Creamy Polenta
flavorProfile: Soft and loose, corn-sweet, finished with a spoon of olive oil rather than butter.
healthBenefit: Cornmeal is naturally gluten-free, and finishing it with olive oil rather than butter keeps the fat mostly unsaturated.
instructions: Bring about three quarters of the water to a high simmer.
Pour the cornmeal in slowly while whisking, so it does not clump, then add the rest of the water.
Simmer for 15 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth.
Off the heat, stir in the olive oil and the salt, cover for 5 minutes and serve hot.

name: Sorghum Pilaf with Vegetables and Pine Nuts
flavorProfile: Chewy and a little nutty, simmered in chicken stock and tossed with carrot, celery, cherry tomatoes and toasted pine nuts.
healthBenefit: Sorghum is a gluten-free whole grain with more fiber than white rice and a low enough glycemic response to sit well beside a light main.

ingredients.prepNote: the sorghum cooks in it; drain any left over
part to toast the sorghum, the rest for the vegetables

ingredients.baseName: Onion, spring (green) or scallion (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Rinse the sorghum and drain it well.
Toast the sorghum with a little of the olive oil in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring all the time, for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly browned.
Add the stock, lower the heat, cover and simmer for 45 to 50 minutes, until the stock is absorbed and the grain is tender. Drain off any liquid left over.
Warm the rest of the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the carrot, celery and garlic for 3 to 5 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Add the green onion, pine nuts and tomatoes and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the nuts start to toast.
Stir in the sorghum and heat it through. Season with the salt and pepper and serve hot with the parsley on top.

name: Coconut Rice
flavorProfile: Fragrant and faintly sweet, with the coconut cooked into the grains rather than poured over them.
healthBenefit: A dairy-free way to get a rich rice side, useful when a main is spicy or acidic and needs something plain beside it.

ingredients.baseName: Rice, long grain, paddy rice, well-milled, raw

instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Put the rice, coconut milk and water in a saucepan and bring them to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes, then fork the salt through.

name: Sweet Potato Mash with Lime and Mint
flavorProfile: Smooth and sweet, with lime juice and fresh mint keeping it from tasting flat.
healthBenefit: Vitamin A and potassium in a soft-textured side, which helps when chewing or digestion is difficult.

ingredients.prepNote: boiled whole in their skins, then peeled
chopped, plus a sprig to garnish

instructions: Put the whole, unpeeled sweet potato in a pot, cover it with water and bring it to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, until it is tender all the way through. Drain it and let it cool enough to handle, then peel it.
Warm the olive oil in the pot over low heat, add the chopped mint and press it into the oil with the back of a spoon.
Add the sweet potato, lime juice, salt and pepper and mash until smooth. Serve with a mint sprig on top.

name: Crunchy Cabbage and Carrot Slaw
flavorProfile: Crunchy and sharp, dressed with lemon and oil instead of mayonnaise.
healthBenefit: Raw cabbage and carrot keep their vitamin C, which cooking would reduce, and the oil helps the carrot beta-carotene absorb.
instructions: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt together in a bowl.
Add the cabbage and carrot and toss until everything is coated.
Serve right away, or keep it covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Cucumber Dill Side Salad
flavorProfile: Cold, crisp and sweet-sour, with red onion and fresh dill through it.
healthBenefit: A high-water side that adds volume and cooling to a heavy plate, with almost nothing in the way of calories.
instructions: Slice the cucumber and the red onion as thinly as you can.
Whisk the vinegar, honey and salt in a bowl until the honey dissolves.
Add the cucumber, onion and dill, season with pepper and toss. Serve, or chill a little first.

name: Apple Fennel Slaw
flavorProfile: Crisp and aromatic, the anise of raw fennel against sweet-tart apple.
healthBenefit: Raw fennel keeps its fiber and potassium, and the lemon juice stops the apple browning without adding anything to it.

ingredients.baseName: Apple, Granny Smith, raw, with skin

instructions: Toss the apple matchsticks with the lemon juice straight away so they do not brown.
Add the fennel, red onion, olive oil and parsley, and season with the salt and pepper.
Toss well and let it sit for 20 minutes before serving.

name: Lemony Greek Chickpeas
flavorProfile: Warm, garlicky and lemony, with cumin, fresh parsley and a sprinkle of sumac.
healthBenefit: Plant protein and soluble fiber in a side that can carry a meal when the main is light.

ingredients.baseName: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), canned, drained, rinsed

ingredients.prepNote: a sprinkle; a Middle Eastern spice no food database lists
ingredients.name: sumac

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the garlic for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the chickpeas, cumin and red pepper flakes, if using, and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, parsley, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with sumac and serve warm.

name: Italian Stewed Lentils (Lenticchie in Umido)
flavorProfile: Soft and savory, the lentils holding their shape with sweet carrot through them.
healthBenefit: Lentils bring plant protein, iron and soluble fiber, and the carrot adds vitamin A to a side substantial enough to stand in for a starch.

ingredients.prepNote: whole, fried with the vegetables and then removed
tied in the herb bundle and removed
tied in the herb bundle and removed
tied in the herb bundle and removed

instructions: Put the lentils in a bowl, cover them with water and throw away any that float. Soak for 2 hours, then drain.
Warm the olive oil in a pot over low heat and cook the carrot, onion, celery and garlic for a few minutes.
Take out the garlic. Add the lentils and stir them for a moment so they take up the flavor.
Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the hot water and add the herb bundle. Do not salt yet, since salt can toughen the skins.
Cover and cook on low heat for 30 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a little water if the pot gets too dry.
Take out the herb bundle, stir in the salt and the pepper if you are using it, and serve warm.

name: Kale Chips
flavorProfile: Thin, salty and brittle, breaking apart the moment you bite one.
healthBenefit: A whole-leaf alternative to a packaged chip, with vitamin K and a fraction of the salt a bagged snack carries.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Strip the leaves off the stems, tear them into chip-sized pieces, and dry them thoroughly. Any water left on them will steam instead of crisping.
Massage the olive oil into the leaves with your hands until every piece has a thin coat.
Spread them on a baking sheet without overlapping and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until they are dry and crisp at the edges.
Salt them as they come out of the oven.

name: Baked Zucchini Chips
flavorProfile: Thin, crisp and faintly sweet, slow-baked until dry all the way through.
healthBenefit: A low-calorie, high-water snack baked rather than fried, so the fat is whatever you brushed on.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 225°F (110°C).
Slice the zucchini as thinly as you can, then lay the slices on paper towel and press another sheet on top to draw out water.
Toss the dried slices with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spread them on a lined baking sheet in one layer and bake for 90 minutes to 2 hours, turning once, until they are dry and crisp.

name: Baked Sweet Potato Chips
flavorProfile: Sweet, salty and snappy, with the edges curling as they crisp.
healthBenefit: Vitamin A and fiber in a chip you bake at home, which keeps the oil to a tablespoon instead of a deep fryer.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 250°F (120°C).
Slice the sweet potato into rounds as thin as you can manage, ideally with a mandoline.
Toss the slices with the olive oil until each one has a thin coat.
Spread them on lined baking sheets in one layer and bake for 1 hour to 90 minutes, turning once, until they are crisp through.
Salt them while they are hot and let them cool before storing.

name: Cucumber Rounds with Tahini
flavorProfile: Cold and crunchy under a nutty, slightly bitter spoon of sesame.
healthBenefit: Tahini brings calcium, magnesium and sesame fat to a vegetable that otherwise carries almost no calories, so the snack holds you longer.
instructions: Cut the cucumber into rounds about a centimeter thick.
Stir the tahini with the lemon juice, grated garlic and salt. It will seize and go stiff first, which is normal.
Add a teaspoon of water at a time, stirring, until it loosens into a spoonable cream.
Spoon a little onto each cucumber round.

name: Rosemary Oat Crackers
flavorProfile: Dry, savory and herbal, snapping cleanly when you break one.
healthBenefit: Oats bring beta-glucan, a soluble fiber tied to cholesterol handling, in a cracker with five ingredients instead of a label full of them.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grind the oats to a coarse flour in a blender or food processor.
Mix the oat flour with the rosemary and salt, then work in the olive oil and water until it forms a stiff dough.
Roll the dough out between two sheets of parchment until it is about 3mm thick, then cut it into squares.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the edges have browned, and let them cool completely so they crisp.

name: Baked Cinnamon Banana Chips
flavorProfile: Thin banana slices baked with cinnamon, nutmeg and a little salt until the edges brown.
healthBenefit: Potassium and fiber from one whole banana, sliced thin and baked with warm spices into a snack for when something sweet is wanted.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 medium, sliced very thin (about ⅛ inch)
a light spray on the foil and the slices; the source gives no amount

instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Peel the banana and slice it very thin, about ⅛ inch.
Line a baking sheet with foil and spray it lightly with oil. Spread out the slices and spray them lightly too.
Mix the cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Sprinkle half over the slices, turn them over and sprinkle the rest.
Bake for about 15 minutes, until the edges are lightly browned. Let them cool for 5 minutes, then peel them off the foil.

name: Cinnamon Apple Slices
flavorProfile: Warm and soft, the apple collapsing slightly with cinnamon through it.
healthBenefit: Apple pectin is a soluble fiber that feeds gut bacteria, and warming the fruit makes it easier to digest than eating it raw.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 medium, cored and sliced, skin on
1 whole clove, taken out before eating

instructions: Core the apple and slice it, leaving the skin on.
Put the slices in a small pan with the water, cinnamon and clove.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes without stirring, until the slices are soft but hold their shape.
Take out the clove. Eat the slices warm, or chill them.

name: Dark Chocolate Orange Date Balls
flavorProfile: Chewy, chocolatey and sweet, with orange juice and zest through the dates and a coat of toasted coconut.
healthBenefit: Dates carry potassium and fiber alongside their sugar, so the sweetness arrives with something slowing it down.

ingredients.prepNote: 3 tablespoons unsweetened flakes, toasted, for rolling

instructions: Put the dates, orange juice, oats, almond butter, cocoa, maple syrup and orange zest in a food processor and blend until the mixture comes together in a sticky dough.
Roll it into 8 balls.
Roll each ball in the toasted coconut and chill for 30 minutes. Keep them in the fridge.

name: Cantaloupe with Lime, Mint and Honey
flavorProfile: Cold, juicy and sharp, with lime, a little honey and fresh mint keeping the melon from tasting flat.
healthBenefit: Cantaloupe is one of the highest vitamin A fruits, and the whole cup is mostly water, which helps on a day you are behind on drinking.
instructions: Cut the cantaloupe into bite-sized cubes and put them in a bowl.
Stir the lime juice, honey and salt together and pour it over the melon.
Scatter the mint over the top, toss gently and chill for 15 minutes before eating.

name: Berry and Coconut Cups
flavorProfile: Tart berries under a spoonful of thick, unsweetened coconut.
healthBenefit: Berry anthocyanins with no added sugar, and coconut milk in place of dairy for anyone avoiding it.
instructions: Chill the can of coconut milk for a few hours and spoon the thick part off the top.
Put the blueberries and halved strawberries in a cup.
Spoon the thick coconut milk over them and eat cold.

name: Pear with Ginger Yogurt
flavorProfile: Soft, sweet pear against cold tangy yogurt with a warm ginger edge.
healthBenefit: Protein from the yogurt with pear fiber, and ginger, which has a long record of settling an unsettled stomach.
instructions: Stir the grated ginger into the yogurt and leave it for 5 minutes so the flavor spreads.
Dice the pear, leaving the skin on for the fiber.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top it with the pear and drizzle the honey over.

name: Grapefruit with Honey
flavorProfile: Sour and bitter, softened by a thin drizzle of honey rather than a spoonful of sugar.
healthBenefit: A serving of grapefruit covers most of a day of vitamin C, and the honey is there in a small enough amount to change the taste without the sugar load.
instructions: Cut the grapefruit in half and run a knife around each segment to free it.
Drizzle the honey over the cut face.
Eat it with a spoon, or lift the segments out into a bowl first.

name: Carrot Sticks with Tahini Dip
flavorProfile: Sweet crunch against a nutty, lemony dip thick enough to hold on the stick.
healthBenefit: Beta-carotene from the carrot absorbs better with the sesame fat in the tahini alongside it.
instructions: Cut the carrots into sticks.
Spoon 6 tablespoons of the Tahini Lemon Sauce into a small bowl. If it has thickened in the fridge, stir in water a teaspoon at a time until it is a dip.
Serve the carrot sticks alongside the bowl.

name: Hummus with Cucumber Spears
flavorProfile: Smooth and lemony, scooped up with cold cucumber instead of bread.
healthBenefit: Plant protein and fiber from the chickpeas, with the cucumber standing in for a cracker, which is where most of the salt in this snack would otherwise come from.
instructions: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt until they are grainy.
With the blender running, pour in the olive oil and then the water until it turns smooth and pale.
Taste it and add lemon juice or salt if it needs it.
Cut the cucumber into spears and serve them with the bowl.

name: Swirled Beet Yogurt Dip with Pepper Strips
flavorProfile: Bright pink and earthy-sweet, with the yogurt keeping it tangy and cool.
healthBenefit: Beet nitrates and yogurt protein together, dipped with red pepper, which is one of the highest vitamin C vegetables by weight.

ingredients.prepNote: about ⅓ teaspoon: a little for the beet, the rest in the yogurt

ingredients.baseName: Yogourt, Greek style, plain, rich (8-12% M.F.)

ingredients.prepNote: flaky salt, a pinch to finish
ingredients.baseName: Fleur de sel, non iodée, non fluorée

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with the olive oil and a small pinch of the salt, cover, and roast for 35 minutes, until a knife goes through easily. Let them cool.
Stir the lemon zest and juice, the rest of the salt and the pepper into the yogurt.
Blend the cooled beet to a smooth purée.
Spread the yogurt in a shallow bowl and swirl the beet purée through it.
Scatter the pistachios, parsley and flaky salt over the top and serve with the pepper strips.

name: Avocado with Lime and Black Pepper
flavorProfile: Rich and buttery, sharpened by lime and lifted by a heavy grind of pepper.
healthBenefit: Monounsaturated fat and potassium, with enough fat to stop a snack turning into hunger an hour later.
instructions: Halve the avocado and take the stone out.
Squeeze the lime juice into the hollow.
Grind the pepper over it and add the salt.
Eat it straight out of the skin with a spoon.

name: Date and Oat Bites
flavorProfile: Dense, chewy and caramel-sweet, with the oats giving them body.
healthBenefit: Oat beta-glucan and date fiber together, which slows how fast the sugar in the dates arrives.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 teaspoon, warm, only if the mixture is crumbly

instructions: Blend the oats in a food processor on high until they look like coarse flour.

Add the dates, maple syrup, cinnamon and salt and keep blending until the crumbs are fine and sticky and hold together when pressed. If they stay crumbly, add the warm water and blend a little longer.
Shape into 9 balls and keep them in the fridge for up to 5 days.

name: Banana Oat Bars
flavorProfile: Soft and cakey, sweet from the banana rather than from added sugar.
healthBenefit: Oat fiber and banana potassium, with maple syrup as the only sweetener and very little of it.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mash the bananas until almost no lumps are left.
Stir in the oats, maple syrup and cinnamon until the mixture is evenly wet.
Press it into a lined small baking dish and bake for 22 to 26 minutes, until the top springs back.
Let it cool completely in the dish before cutting, or the bars will fall apart.

name: Coconut Date Balls
flavorProfile: Sweet and rich, with coconut running through the chew.
healthBenefit: Fiber and potassium from the dates, with coconut fat slowing the sugar, and no dairy or grain in it at all.

ingredients.prepNote: for rolling, about 3 tablespoons; the source gives no amount

instructions: Put the almonds, dates, coconut oil and desiccated coconut in a food processor and run it on high until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Roll tablespoon-sized pieces into balls, then roll each in the shredded coconut.
Set them on a lined tray and chill for at least 30 minutes to firm up. Keep them in the fridge.

name: Maple Oat Clusters
flavorProfile: Toasted and crunchy, breaking into clumps rather than loose grains.
healthBenefit: A granola you control the sugar in: about four tablespoons of maple syrup across the whole batch instead of what a boxed one carries.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 325°F (160°C).
Stir the oats with the maple syrup, olive oil, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until every oat is coated.
Press the mixture into a flat layer on a lined baking sheet, which is what makes it clump instead of scatter.
Bake for about 25 minutes without stirring, until it is golden.
Let it cool completely on the sheet, then break it into clusters.
